methodology.name: Sentinel-As-Code maturity assessment
methodology.scaleNote: Computed from deployed configuration and 30 days of activity; a reference point for prioritising work, not an audit or a risk rating.

areas.name: Detection engineering
areas.description: Rules exist, are maintained, map entities and produce incidents worth having.

criteria.name: Analytics rules are deployed and enabled
criteria.impact: Without enabled rules nothing in the workspace produces an incident.
criteria.guidance: Enable the Content Hub rule templates for the connected data sources, starting with the High-severity ones.

criteria.name: Custom detections exist alongside templates
criteria.evidence: 1 enabled rule(s) authored without a template.
criteria.impact: Templates cover the generic cases; custom rules are where organisation-specific risk gets detected.
criteria.guidance: Write Scheduled or NRT rules for the risks the templates do not cover (business applications, privileged workflows, crown-jewel systems) and keep them in source control.

criteria.name: Enabled rules map entities
criteria.impact: Incidents without entities cannot be investigated through the graph, grouped by entity or enriched by UEBA.
criteria.guidance: Add entity mappings (account, host, IP) to every Scheduled and NRT rule.

criteria.name: Rules are reviewed within twelve months
criteria.impact: Rules nobody has touched in a year drift away from the environment they were written for.
criteria.guidance: Review every enabled rule at least yearly: query still valid, thresholds still right, data source still present.

criteria.name: No rules left disabled
criteria.impact: A disabled rule is coverage someone decided to switch off; without a reason recorded it is a silent gap.
criteria.guidance: Re-enable or delete disabled rules; if a rule must stay off, record why in its description.

criteria.name: False-positive rate is under control
criteria.impact: Rules that mostly produce false positives train analysts to ignore them.
criteria.guidance: Tune or retire rules whose closed incidents are mostly false positives; the per-rule effectiveness table shows which.

criteria.name: Content is current
criteria.evidence: Installed solutions are out of date or deprecated.
criteria.impact: Out-of-date or deprecated solutions miss the detections Microsoft has shipped since.
criteria.guidance: Update installed Content Hub solutions and replace deprecated ones.

criteria.name: Legacy incident-creation rules retired
criteria.impact: Legacy Microsoft incident-creation rules duplicate what the Defender XDR connector now does.
criteria.guidance: Enable incident sync on the Defender XDR connector and disable the legacy rules.

areas.name: Platform and collection
areas.description: The workspace and its collection pipeline are current, governed and resilient.

criteria.name: Collection is governed by data collection rules
criteria.impact: DCRs are where ingestion-time filtering and transformation live; without them every byte lands as sent.
criteria.guidance: Move agent and API collection onto DCRs so filters and transforms can be applied before ingestion.

criteria.name: No legacy custom log (CLv1) tables
criteria.impact: CLv1 tables stop accepting data when the HTTP Data Collector API retires; transforms and DCR routing never apply to them.
criteria.guidance: Migrate each CLv1 table to a DCR-based custom table.

criteria.name: Agents migrated off the Log Analytics agent
criteria.impact: The Log Analytics agent is retired; machines still on it are on borrowed time.
criteria.guidance: Move every machine to the Azure Monitor Agent and remove the MMA extension.

criteria.name: Query audit logging is on
criteria.impact: Without LAQueryLogs there is no record of who ran what against the security data.
criteria.guidance: Enable the Audit diagnostic category on the workspace so LAQueryLogs populates.

criteria.name: Workspace replication is enabled
criteria.impact: Without replication a regional outage takes the SOC's data and detections with it.
criteria.guidance: Enable workspace replication to a secondary region.

criteria.name: Ingestion and query use private networking
criteria.impact: Public endpoints expose the workspace to credential-based access from anywhere.
criteria.guidance: Disable public network access for ingestion and query and route through an Azure Monitor Private Link Scope.

criteria.name: Connector health is clean
criteria.evidence: 8 connector failure(s) in SentinelHealth in 7 days.
criteria.impact: Failed data-fetcher runs mean a connector is silently dropping data.
criteria.guidance: Investigate every connector failure in SentinelHealth and fix the credential, permission or endpoint behind it.

areas.name: Telemetry coverage
areas.description: The sources an investigation needs are connected and producing data.

criteria.name: Telemetry is being ingested
criteria.impact: An empty workspace detects nothing.
criteria.guidance: Connect the data sources the detections need.

criteria.name: Identity telemetry is present
criteria.evidence: 1 Entra ID table(s) ingesting in the last 7 days.
criteria.impact: Most intrusions go through identity; without sign-in and audit logs they are invisible.
criteria.guidance: Connect the Microsoft Entra ID connector with sign-in, audit and non-interactive sign-in logs.

criteria.name: Endpoint and XDR telemetry is present
criteria.impact: Without Defender XDR tables there is no endpoint, email or cloud-app visibility to correlate with.
criteria.guidance: Connect Defender XDR and enable the advanced hunting tables (Device*, Email*, CloudAppEvents, Identity*).

criteria.name: Cloud posture alerts flow in
criteria.impact: Defender for Cloud alerts are the only signal for many resource-level attacks.
criteria.guidance: Connect the Microsoft Defender for Cloud connector so its alerts become incidents.

criteria.name: UEBA is enabled
criteria.evidence: UEBA is enabled and producing data.
criteria.impact: Without UEBA there are no behavioural baselines, no peer analytics and no entity insights.
criteria.guidance: Enable UEBA on the Entra ID and, where present, Active Directory sources.

criteria.name: Entity analytics is enabled
criteria.impact: Entity analytics feeds the entity pages and IdentityInfo that investigations lean on.
criteria.guidance: Enable the Entity Analytics setting with at least the Entra ID provider.

areas.name: Automation and response
areas.description: Triage, enrichment and response run without an analyst at the keyboard.

criteria.name: Automation rules exist
criteria.impact: Without automation rules every incident is triaged by hand from a cold start.
criteria.guidance: Start with automation rules that assign owners, tag by tactic and suppress known-benign patterns.

criteria.name: Playbooks run reliably
criteria.impact: A failing playbook is a response step that is quietly not happening.
criteria.guidance: Fix playbooks with failed runs and alert on automation health.

criteria.name: Playbooks are deployed
criteria.impact: Playbooks are how enrichment, notification and containment happen without an analyst at the keyboard.
criteria.guidance: Deploy playbooks for enrichment and notification first, containment once the SOC trusts them.

criteria.name: Watchlists are in use
criteria.impact: Watchlists hold the allow-lists, VIP lists and asset context that keep detections precise.
criteria.guidance: Create watchlists for known-good sources, high-value assets and service accounts and reference them in rules.

areas.name: Monitoring coverage
areas.description: What is ingested is watched, across the kill chain and the platform itself.

criteria.name: Enabled rules create incidents
criteria.impact: Alert-only rules fire into a void unless something else consumes the alert.
criteria.guidance: Enable incident creation on rules that are not purely feeding correlation.

criteria.name: Sentinel health is tracked
criteria.impact: Without SentinelHealth data there is no record of connector, rule or automation failures.
criteria.guidance: Enable the Sentinel health diagnostic setting so SentinelHealth populates.

criteria.name: Broad MITRE tactic coverage
criteria.evidence: Only 2 of 14 MITRE tactics have an enabled rule.
criteria.impact: Coverage concentrated on two or three tactics leaves the rest of the kill chain unobserved.
criteria.guidance: Deploy or write rules for the tactics with the fewest detections; the MITRE coverage page lists them.

criteria.name: No tactic without a rule
criteria.impact: A tactic with zero rules is a stage of an attack nothing is watching.
criteria.guidance: Give every tactic at least one enabled rule.

criteria.name: Ingested data has detections
criteria.impact: Tables nothing reads are cost without coverage.
criteria.guidance: Deploy templates or write rules for the high-volume tables no rule reads, or move them to a cheaper tier.

areas.name: Incident management
areas.description: Incidents are acknowledged, worked, classified and closed in time.

criteria.name: Incidents are being closed
criteria.impact: An incident queue that only grows means triage has stopped.
criteria.guidance: Work the queue; automate closure of known-benign patterns.

criteria.name: Incidents are classified on closure
criteria.impact: Without a verdict on closure there is no false-positive rate and no basis for tuning.
criteria.guidance: Make a true, benign or false positive verdict mandatory when closing.

criteria.name: Mean time to acknowledge under four hours
criteria.evidence: Mean time to acknowledge is 95.5 minutes.
criteria.impact: Slow acknowledgement is dwell time handed to the attacker.
criteria.guidance: Route high-severity incidents to an on-call rota and measure MTTA weekly.

criteria.name: Detections produce incidents
criteria.impact: No incidents in 30 days means either nothing is being detected or nothing is creating incidents.
criteria.guidance: Confirm rules are enabled, creating incidents and reading tables that have data.

criteria.name: Closures are acknowledged
criteria.impact: Incidents closed without ever being acknowledged were never looked at.
criteria.guidance: Stop auto-closing without review; have automation assign before it closes.

criteria.name: Mean time to resolve within target
criteria.impact: Long resolution times extend the impact window.
criteria.guidance: Set a resolution target per severity and review the incidents that miss it.

areas.name: Investigation and evidence
areas.description: Evidence is complete, retained and recoverable when an investigation needs it.

criteria.name: Retention matches ingestion
criteria.impact: Tables that have gone silent or exist with no data are investigation dead ends.
criteria.guidance: Fix silent tables and remove orphan tables.

criteria.name: Search or restore has been exercised
criteria.evidence: No search jobs or restores on record.
criteria.impact: If long-term data has never been searched or restored, nobody knows whether it can be.
criteria.guidance: Run a search job or a restore against archived data at least quarterly.

criteria.name: Evidence is recoverable beyond interactive retention
criteria.evidence: No table has retention beyond the interactive window and no restore has been run.
criteria.impact: Investigations that reach back past interactive retention need a long-term tier or a working restore path.
criteria.guidance: Extend total retention on the evidential tables or move them to the data lake tier, and prove the restore path.

areas.name: Threat intelligence
areas.description: Indicators arrive from more than one source and detections read the current schema.

criteria.name: Off the legacy indicator table
criteria.impact: The legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table stopped receiving indicators on 31 July 2025.
criteria.guidance: Move ingestion to the upload API or TAXII, into ThreatIntelIndicators.

criteria.name: Rules read the current indicator schema
criteria.impact: Rules on the legacy table match against an expiring set of indicators and go quiet.
criteria.guidance: Rewrite TI rules to read ThreatIntelIndicators.

criteria.name: Indicators are arriving
criteria.impact: TI detections with no indicators to match are decorative.
criteria.guidance: Connect a feed and confirm indicators land in ThreatIntelIndicators.

criteria.name: STIX objects are present
criteria.evidence: 1,512 STIX object(s) in ThreatIntelObjects over 30 days.
criteria.impact: Objects beyond indicators (threat actors, attack patterns, relationships) give matches their context.
criteria.guidance: Use a feed or the upload API that supplies STIX objects, not indicators alone.

criteria.name: More than one feed
criteria.impact: A single feed is a single point of failure for every TI detection.
criteria.guidance: Add a second source: Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence, a TAXII collection or the upload API.

criteria.name: Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence is active
criteria.evidence: MDTI connector or MDTI indicators present.
criteria.impact: MDTI is the lowest-effort feed, with Microsoft's own indicators.
criteria.guidance: Enable the Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence connector.

areas.name: Threat hunting
areas.description: Hunting is recorded, resourced with content and feeds detection engineering.

criteria.name: Hunts are recorded
criteria.impact: Hunting that is not recorded cannot be repeated, measured or turned into detections.
criteria.guidance: Run hunts through the Hunts feature with a hypothesis and an outcome.

criteria.name: Findings are bookmarked
criteria.impact: Bookmarks are how a hunting result becomes evidence on an incident.
criteria.guidance: Bookmark notable results and promote them to incidents where warranted.

criteria.name: Hunting content is available
criteria.impact: Without hunting queries each hunt starts from a blank editor.
criteria.guidance: Deploy the hunting queries from the Content Hub solutions for the connected sources.

criteria.name: Hunting library of 25 or more
criteria.impact: A broad library lets hunters pivot across tactics and sources.
criteria.guidance: Grow the library past 25 queries, covering every connected data source.

areas.name: Log management and cost
areas.description: Retention, tiers and caps are set deliberately rather than left at defaults.

criteria.name: Per-table retention is tuned
criteria.evidence: 2 table(s) with retention set away from the workspace default.
criteria.impact: One retention for everything over-pays on noisy tables and under-keeps the evidential ones.
criteria.guidance: Set retention per table: short for high-volume operational logs, long for identity and audit.

criteria.name: Table tiers are used
criteria.impact: High-volume tables on the Analytics tier that no rule needs are the main cost lever left unpulled.
criteria.guidance: Move verbose, investigation-only tables to Basic or Data Lake.

criteria.name: A daily cap is set
criteria.impact: Without a cap a runaway connector bills without limit.
criteria.guidance: Set a daily cap at around 110% of expected ingestion and alert on it.

criteria.name: Long-term tier in use
criteria.evidence: No table has retention beyond the interactive window.
criteria.impact: Evidence older than the interactive window is lost without a long-term tier.
criteria.guidance: Set total retention beyond interactive retention on evidential tables, or mirror them to the data lake.

criteria.name: Summary rules are used
criteria.impact: Summary rules turn verbose tables into cheap aggregates that detections and workbooks can read.
criteria.guidance: Create summary rules for the high-volume tables whose detail is rarely needed.

criteria.name: No duplicate firewall logging
criteria.impact: Azure Firewall logged to both legacy and structured tables is billed twice.
criteria.guidance: Remove the legacy AzureDiagnostics categories once rules read the AZFW tables.

areas.name: Governance and access
areas.description: Access follows least privilege and the workspace is protected from accidents.

criteria.name: Workspace access follows least privilege
criteria.evidence: 2 Owner or Contributor assignment(s) at workspace scope.
criteria.impact: Owner and Contributor at workspace scope can change or delete every detection.
criteria.guidance: Replace broad roles with the Microsoft Sentinel roles; keep Owner and Contributor to a handful of break-glass identities.

criteria.name: Sentinel roles are used
criteria.evidence: 1 Microsoft Sentinel role assignment(s) at workspace scope.
criteria.impact: If nobody holds a Microsoft Sentinel role, access is being granted through broader Azure roles.
criteria.guidance: Assign Microsoft Sentinel Reader, Responder and Contributor to the SOC groups.

criteria.name: Workspace is protected by a delete lock
criteria.impact: A workspace deleted by mistake takes the SOC's history with it.
criteria.guidance: Add a CanNotDelete lock on the workspace.

criteria.name: Responder role is assigned
criteria.impact: Without Responder assignments analysts act through broader roles or cannot act at all.
criteria.guidance: Assign Microsoft Sentinel Responder to the analyst group.

criteria.name: No service principal holds Owner or Contributor
criteria.impact: A compromised deployment identity with Contributor can rewrite every detection.
criteria.guidance: Give deployment identities Microsoft Sentinel Contributor and Log Analytics Contributor rather than Owner or Contributor.

subcategories.outcome: Potentially adverse events are analysed to better understand associated activities.
Information is correlated from multiple sources.
Information on adverse events is provided to authorised staff and tools.
Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis.
Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria.
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Computing hardware and software, runtime environments and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established, communicated and enforced.
Roles, responsibilities and authorities for cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood and enforced.
Systems, hardware, software, services and data are managed throughout their life cycles.
Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises.
Improvements are identified from the execution of operational processes, procedures and activities.
Cyber threat intelligence is received from information-sharing forums and sources.
Internal and external threats to the organisation are identified and recorded.
Access permissions, entitlements and authorisations are defined in policy, managed, enforced and reviewed, incorporating least privilege and separation of duties.
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data at rest are protected.
Backups of data are created, protected, maintained and tested.
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorised logical access and usage.
Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained.
Configuration management practices are established and applied.
Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration.
Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause.
Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved.
Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved.
Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents.
The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared.
Incident reports are triaged and validated.
Incidents are categorised and prioritised.
Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed.
Incidents are contained.
Incidents are eradicated.

outOfScope.reason: Only the parts that leave a trace in the workspace (automation rules, hunts, classifications) are assessed.
No reliable signal in the captured configuration.

outOfScope.area: Automation coverage of specific incident types
outOfScope.reason: Incident data is captured in aggregate only.
